title: Идея с кабинетом и сломанный слив  (The Office Couch Idea and the Broken Drain)

segments.t: Senya and Fedya point out that Chef Barinov has a luxurious leather couch right in his private office where nobody will bother them after closing. Meanwhile, Vika catches Kostya and Nastya emerging from the guest restroom and buys their excuse about a broken drain.
Аркадий, а ты все видел и молчал?
Там слив сломался, а мы его...
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'You could bring her right here to the couch.' The grammar packs 'on' and 'here' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'It is a magnificent couch.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'splendid' and finishing on 'sofa'.
'Why not?' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'what' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'In my own office?' In Russian, the idea of 'mine' flows naturally into 'office' without extra filler words.
'Right here in my restaurant.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'restaurant' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Very convenient.' Kostya anchors the line on 'very', while 'comfortable' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Nobody is around.' In Russian, the idea of 'nobody' flows naturally into 'there is no' without extra filler words.
Аркадий, а ты все видел и молчал?
'Arkady, you saw everything and kept quiet?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Arkady' before landing on 'to be silent'.
'At least Arkady did not join in.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'participated' places the action in the masculine past tense. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'There is a separate restroom for staff members.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'for' and finishing on 'restroom'.
'What is going on here?' Vika brings out the contrast between 'what' and 'matter' in a few short words.
'Hello, Viktoriya Sergeyevna.' The meaning hinges on 'hello' working together with 'Sergeyevna' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Там слив сломался, а мы его...

'The drain broke in there, and we were just...' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'broke down' places the action in the masculine past tense. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Аркадий, а ты все видел и молчал?
Там слив сломался, а мы его...

That wraps up this scene as senya and Fedya suggest that Chef Barinov bring Elena Pavlovna to the leather couch in his office after hours, while Vika catches Kostya and Nastya in the guest restroom. Until next time!
